---
title: "The Robbery Leaderboard"
subtitle: "Every UFC decision, ranked by how strongly the statistics disagree with the result"
---

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
source("_common.R")
tb <- rd("tiers")
mt <- rd("media_by_tier")
```

The **Robbery Score** is 1 − P(declared winner wins | fight stats). A high score means the round-by-round statistics strongly favoured the fighter who lost. It does *not* mean the judges were wrong: stats can't see damage, power or octagon control. That's why every row also shows how the **media** scored the fight, and why some rows carry a *limited corroboration* flag (fights before 2008, when stats were coded from video years later, or fights with fewer than 3 media scores).

## Tiers

```{r}
#| label: tiers
tb |> mutate(tier = factor(tier, names(tier_cols))) |> arrange(tier) |>
  left_join(mt |> select(tier, media_majority_loser), by = "tier") |>
  transmute(Tier = tier,
            `Score range` = c("< 0.25", "0.25–0.50", "0.50–0.75", "≥ 0.75")[as.integer(tier)],
            Decisions = n, Share = share, `Media majority scored it for the loser*` = media_majority_loser) |>
  gt() |>
  fmt_number(Decisions, decimals = 0) |>
  fmt_percent(c(Share, `Media majority scored it for the loser*`), decimals = 1) |>
  tab_footnote("* Among decisions with at least 5 media scorecards.") |>
  opt_row_striping()
```

The tiers are the cutoffs fixed before looking at the media data (0.25 / 0.50 / 0.75). Media agreement rises steadily across them, which is what a meaningful scale should do.

```{r}
#| label: distribution
#| fig-alt: "Histogram of Robbery Scores coloured by tier"
plot_robbery_distribution(ri)
```

## Search every decision

Click a row to see why the model disagrees. Cards list the declared winner's total first.

```{r}
#| label: table
tier_badge <- function(t) {
  col <- tier_cols[[t]]
  htmltools::span(class = "tier-pill", style = paste0("background:", col, ";",
                  if (t %in% c("Clean", "Close / defensible")) "color:#1B1F24;" else ""), t)
}
tbl <- ri |>
  arrange(desc(robbery_score)) |>
  transmute(Date = date, Event = event, Winner = winner_name, Loser = loser_name,
            Decision = coalesce(decision_type, "Draw"), Cards = cards_winner_first,
            Score = robbery_score, Tier = as.character(tier), `P(winner)` = p_winner,
            `Media for loser` = if_else(coalesce(media_scored, 0) > 0,
                                        paste0(media_for_loser, "/", media_scored), "–"),
            Flag = if_else(limited_corroboration, "Limited corroboration", ""),
            why = coalesce(why, "Draw: no declared winner."))
reactable(
  tbl, searchable = TRUE, filterable = FALSE, striped = TRUE, highlight = TRUE, compact = TRUE,
  defaultPageSize = 20, showPageSizeOptions = TRUE, pageSizeOptions = c(20, 50, 100),
  defaultSorted = list(Score = "desc"),
  columns = list(
    Date = colDef(format = colFormat(date = TRUE), width = 100),
    Event = colDef(minWidth = 180),
    Cards = colDef(minWidth = 220, style = list(fontSize = "0.8rem")),
    Score = colDef(format = colFormat(digits = 3), width = 80,
                   style = function(v) list(fontWeight = if (!is.na(v) && v >= 0.75) 700 else 400)),
    Tier = colDef(cell = function(v) if (is.na(v)) "Draw" else tier_badge(v), width = 140),
    `P(winner)` = colDef(format = colFormat(percent = TRUE, digits = 0), width = 90),
    `Media for loser` = colDef(width = 90, align = "center"),
    Flag = colDef(width = 120, style = list(fontSize = "0.75rem", color = "#6B7280")),
    why = colDef(show = FALSE)
  ),
  details = function(i) htmltools::div(style = "padding: 0.6rem 1rem; font-size: 0.9rem;", tbl$why[i])
)
```

## Top 25

```{r}
#| label: top25
top25 <- ri_nd |> arrange(desc(robbery_score)) |> head(25)
top25 |>
  transmute(Rank = row_number(), Date = date, Bout = fight_label(winner_name, loser_name),
            Decision = decision_type, Cards = cards_winner_first, `Robbery Score` = robbery_score,
            `P(loser wins)` = p_loser,
            `Media for loser` = if_else(coalesce(media_scored, 0) > 0, paste0(media_for_loser, " of ", media_scored), "–"),
            `Limited corroboration` = if_else(limited_corroboration, "Yes", "")) |>
  gt() |>
  fmt_date(Date, date_style = "yMMMd") |>
  fmt_number(`Robbery Score`, decimals = 3) |>
  fmt_percent(`P(loser wins)`, decimals = 0) |>
  data_color(`Robbery Score`, palette = c("#F2C4CB", "#8E0C22"), domain = c(0.75, 1)) |>
  tab_style(cell_text(size = "small"), cells_body(columns = Cards)) |>
  opt_row_striping()
```

## The top 10, explained

```{r}
#| label: top10
#| results: asis
top10 <- head(top25, 10)
for (i in seq_len(nrow(top10))) {
  x <- top10[i, ]
  media <- if (coalesce(x$media_scored, 0) > 0)
    sprintf(" Media: %d of %d scorecards had %s winning.", x$media_for_loser, x$media_scored, x$loser_name) else
    " No media scorecards are recorded for this fight."
  flag <- if (x$limited_corroboration) " *Limited corroboration: treat with extra caution.*" else ""
  cat(sprintf("**%d. %s** (%s, %s; %s decision). Robbery Score **%.3f**. %s%s%s\n\n",
              i, fight_label(x$winner_name, x$loser_name), x$event, format(x$date, "%b %d, %Y"),
              tolower(x$decision_type), x$robbery_score, x$why, media, flag))
}
```

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
## Reading a high score
A high score with **strong media support** for the loser (for example 80–100% of media scorecards) is the clearest kind of disagreement. A high score with **little media support** usually means the people watching saw something the counts don't record: damage, power, or which strikes actually landed clean. Those cases are listed on the [Validation](validation.qmd) page.
:::
